content.title: Want to Make Winter the ‘Spring’ of Your Amal?
content.subtitle: Discover 5 special deeds to earn immense rewards with little effort right now.
content.body:
A believer is always looking for ways to become beloved to Allah by earning vast rewards with minimal hardship. The righteous predecessors (Salaf) used to call winter "the springtime of the believer"—because its short days make fasting effortless, and its long nights offer abundant opportunities for worship.

Let us explore 5 special winter Amal that will weigh heavily on your scale of good actions:

1. Donating Winter Clothes to Those in Need

During the biting cold, the helpless and destitute suffer immensely. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most beloved people to Allah are those who are most beneficial to others."

Stand by those shivering in the cold according to your capacity. Even if your means are modest, spending a small amount on a muffler or a pair of gloves—solely for the pleasure of Allah—can bring immense reward.

2. Observing Voluntary Fasts (Nafl Sawm)

Because winter days are short and thirst is minimal, fasting becomes remarkably easy. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Fasting in winter is an effortless spoil (Ghanimah)."

Take advantage of this season to observe the Sunnah fasts on Mondays and Thursdays, the White Days (Ayyam al-Beed—the 13th, 14th, and 15th of the lunar month), or to make up any missed Ramadan fasts. It is also an ideal time to gently train young children in the habit of fasting before Ramadan arrives.

3. Praying Tahajjud in the Long Nights

Since winter nights are long, going to bed by 10 or 11 PM allows you to get plenty of rest and still wake up easily before Fajr.

According to a narration, when a servant leaves the warmth of their bed on a freezing night, performs Wudu, and stands in prayer, Allah smiles with pleasure at them. Scholars explain this refers to both Tahajjud and Fajr prayers—and whomever Allah smiles upon with pleasure is guaranteed Paradise!

4. Performing Wudu Thoroughly Despite the Cold

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked his Companions: "Shall I not tell you of something by which Allah erases sins and elevates ranks? It is performing Wudu thoroughly during difficult times (such as severe cold)..."

Many people, out of fear of cold water, reduce their water intake or hold back the urge to relieve themselves just to pray Isha with their Asr Wudu. This harms one's health and destroys Khushu (focus) in prayer. Do not hold back your Wudu—embrace the cold water hoping for Allah's reward.

5. Remembering Hellfire Amid the Bitter Cold

Authentic narrations inform us that when Hellfire complained to its Lord, Allah permitted it to take two breaths each year: one in the summer (intense heat) and one in the winter (intense cold).

Therefore, whenever you feel the harshness of winter, seek refuge with Allah from Zamharir—the severe, freezing punishment of Hell—and focus on deeds that save you from the Fire.

Do not let these blessed winter days slip away in idleness beneath a warm blanket. Start striving for your Lord’s love today through these simple, rewarding deeds. May Allah grant us the ability to act upon them. Ameen.

References:

  1. Sahih al-Bukhari: Hadith 537

  1. Sahih Muslim: Hadiths 251, 560

  1. Jami' at-Tirmidhi: Hadith 797

  1. Musnad Ahmad: Hadith 3949
